c.tagline: Wales's compact capital of castles, choirs, and rugby roar.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed Hackney (black/blue) cabs are metered and can be hailed or picked up at ranks; private-hire cars such as Dragon Taxis and app rides (Uber, Bolt) must be pre-booked.

emergency.note: 112 works throughout the UK and Europe and connects to police, fire, and ambulance; 999 is the traditional UK emergency number.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The St Mary Street nightlife strip gets rowdy with drunken crowds late on weekends and rugby match days.

hood_desc: The walkable heart around Cardiff Castle, the Principality Stadium, the covered Victorian arcades and St David's shopping centre; best for first-timers who want everything on the doorstep.
Cardiff Bay (Butetown): a redeveloped waterfront around Mermaid Quay and the Wales Millennium Centre, with restaurants, bars, and boat trips; good for waterside dining and evenings out.
A leafy, village-like district of Victorian terraces, independent cafes, delis, and Pontcanna Fields; suits travellers wanting a relaxed, foodie, local base a short walk from the centre.
The student quarter beside Cardiff University and the Civic Centre's museums; lively, budget-friendly, and very central.
A residential area around Roath Park and its boating lake, with the Wellfield Road cafes and independent shops; calm and family-friendly.
lodging: voco St. David's Cardiff by IHG

water.note: Tap water is safe and good quality.

transit.hours: Cardiff Bus services run from roughly 5:00 AM to around 11:00 PM, with some late-night routes on weekends; Transport for Wales trains run from early morning to late evening.
transit.note: Cardiff Bus is the main city operator, with Transport for Wales running local rail (the Valley Lines network) from Cardiff Central and Queen Street stations. The compact centre and Cardiff Bay are easily walked or reached by a short bus or train hop.
transit.pay: Pay the bus driver by contactless card or cash, or use the Cardiff Bus app; trains are paid by ticket, contactless, or the TfW app. Multi-operator day tickets allow unlimited travel across city bus routes.

bus: National Express & Megabus coaches from Sophia Gardens / Kingsway

car.idp: Not required for short visits (EU/US licences accepted)

train: Cardiff Central & Cardiff Queen Street (Transport for Wales and GWR; direct trains to London Paddington and the Valley Lines local network)

transit.m: T9 Cardiff Airport Express bus to city centre (~40 min)
905 shuttle to Rhoose station then train to Cardiff Central (~50 min)

tip.r: Around 10% at restaurants is common if a service charge isn't already added; rounding up the fare for taxis.
